type1.name: The Reformer
type1.description: Type 1s are principled, purposeful, self-controlled, and perfectionistic. They strive to be right, to live correctly, and to improve the world. They are conscientious and have strong values, but can become critical and demanding of themselves and others.
strengths: Strong sense of purpose and ethics
Conscientious and responsible
Excellent at improving systems and processes
Principled and fair in decision-making
Dedicated to quality and excellence
Self-disciplined and organized
Advocates for positive change
weaknesses: Tendency to be overly critical and judgmental
Can be rigid and perfectionistic
Difficulty accepting mistakes in themselves and others
May suppress emotions in pursuit of being 'right'
Can experience significant inner tension and frustration
May seem cold or overly serious to others
Struggle with self-compassion and flexibility
relationshipTips: Remember that perfection is impossible - practice accepting 'good enough'
Express your values clearly but without judgment of others
Balance your idealism with compassion for human fallibility
Show appreciation for your partner's efforts, not just results
Learn to relax and enjoy life without needing improvement
growthAreas: Develop self-compassion and accept your own imperfections
Practice seeing the good in situations, not just flaws
Learn to let go of the need to control or improve everything
Recognize that different approaches can be equally valid
Balance critique with appreciation and encouragement
Allow yourself to experience emotions without judging them
Remember that being human means being imperfect

type2.name: The Helper
type2.description: Type 2s are empathetic, sincere, warm-hearted, and relationship-focused. They are generous givers who find meaning in helping others. However, they can become overly focused on others' needs at the expense of their own, and may struggle with resentment when help isn't reciprocated.
strengths: Genuinely caring and empathetic toward others
Excellent at building meaningful relationships
Generous and willing to help without expecting reward
Strong emotional intelligence and intuition
Natural ability to understand others' needs
Warm and welcoming to those around them
Dedicated and loyal in relationships
weaknesses: Tendency to neglect their own needs while helping others
Can become overly focused on others' approval
Struggle with setting boundaries
May feel resentment when help isn't reciprocated
Can be manipulative in subtle ways
Difficulty asking for help or expressing needs
May lose sense of self in relationships
relationshipTips: Your generosity is beautiful - make sure to receive care too
Communicate your needs directly rather than expecting others to guess
Practice saying 'no' without guilt or resentment
Remember that taking care of yourself helps you help others better
Don't keep score of favors - help because you want to, not for payback
growthAreas: Learn to prioritize your own wellbeing equally with others'
Develop healthy boundaries in relationships
Practice expressing your needs clearly and directly
Challenge the belief that love equals self-sacrifice
Recognize that you are worthy of care and attention too
Build independence and a strong sense of self
Learn that others must take responsibility for themselves

type3.name: The Achiever
type3.description: Type 3s are success-oriented, adaptive, and excellent at accomplishing goals. They are driven by the desire to be valuable and to gain recognition. However, they can become overly focused on image and external validation, losing touch with their authentic selves.
strengths: Highly motivated and goal-oriented
Excellent problem-solvers and action-takers
Adaptive and able to adjust approach based on feedback
Natural leaders who inspire others through example
Efficient and productive in accomplishing tasks
Charming and socially adept
Resilient and competitive in healthy ways
weaknesses: Can be overly focused on image and external success
May neglect personal relationships in pursuit of goals
Difficulty being authentic or vulnerable
Can be workaholic and driven by external validation
May struggle with knowing who they are beyond achievements
Can be competitive in unhealthy or cutthroat ways
Difficulty tolerating failure or setbacks
relationshipTips: Make dedicated time for relationships, not just when convenient
Be authentic with your partner - show your real self, not your image
Remember that your worth isn't tied to achievements
Share your vulnerabilities and fears, not just successes
Listen to your partner without planning your response
growthAreas: Develop a sense of self based on internal values, not external success
Learn to be vulnerable and authentic in relationships
Practice measuring success by personal growth, not just achievement
Challenge the belief that you must earn love through accomplishments
Develop compassion for yourself when you fail or underperform
Learn to slow down and enjoy the present moment
Remember that being human is enough - you don't need to earn your value

type4.name: The Individualist
type4.description: Type 4s are self-aware, sensitive, and emotionally expressive. They crave authenticity and deep meaning. They are creative and introspective, but can become self-absorbed, moody, and overly focused on what's missing in their lives.
strengths: Highly creative and artistic abilities
Deep emotional awareness and authenticity
Strong sense of individuality and uniqueness
Excellent at understanding complex emotions
Natural ability to empathize with others' pain
Passionate about meaningful self-expression
Able to find beauty in sadness and struggle
weaknesses: Tendency toward melancholy and focusing on what's missing
Can be overly self-absorbed and self-conscious
Difficulty tolerating ordinary, everyday life
May withdraw when hurt instead of communicating
Can be dramatic or overly emotional
Struggle with shame and feeling fundamentally flawed
May idealize relationships unrealistically
relationshipTips: Your depth and authenticity are gifts - share them
Remember that your partner can't fix the emptiness - only you can
Express feelings directly rather than through withdrawal
Appreciate the ordinary moments, not just the intense ones
Don't idealize your partner - see and love them as they are
growthAreas: Learn to find meaning in ordinary experiences, not just intense ones
Develop appreciation for what you have instead of what's missing
Practice self-acceptance and stop comparing yourself to others
Engage with the world despite feeling different or misunderstood
Balance introspection with action and connection
Challenge the belief that suffering equals depth
Remember that you are fundamentally okay just as you are

type5.name: The Investigator
type5.description: Type 5s are perceptive, innovative, and focused on understanding the world. They are curious and analytical, thriving on knowledge and competence. However, they can become detached, isolated, and overly cerebral, disconnecting from their emotions and relationships.
strengths: Highly intelligent and curious about how things work
Excellent researchers and innovators
Able to see connections and patterns others miss
Independent and self-sufficient thinkers
Deep knowledge and expertise in areas of interest
Objective and analytical in problem-solving
Thoughtful and careful in decision-making
weaknesses: Tendency to withdraw and isolate from others
Can be detached and emotionally unavailable
May become obsessed with information gathering
Difficulty with practical implementation
Can seem cold or disinterested in others
Struggle with social connection and small talk
May feel overwhelmed in social situations
relationshipTips: Make effort to engage emotionally, not just intellectually
Share your thoughts and feelings regularly
Spend time with others even when you prefer solitude
Remember that relationships require presence and attention
Practice small talk and social connection
growthAreas: Develop emotional awareness and expression
Challenge the belief that emotions are irrational
Learn to balance thinking with feeling and doing
Practice being present with others without needing to understand everything
Engage with people and the world despite uncertainty
Remember that you can be competent and still need others
Develop comfort with not knowing everything

type6.name: The Loyalist
type6.description: Type 6s are reliable, committed, and security-oriented. They are conscientious and questioning, wanting to understand systems and predict problems. However, they can become anxious, suspicious, and overly focused on worst-case scenarios.
strengths: Loyal and devoted in relationships and commitments
Excellent at anticipating problems and planning for contingencies
Reliable and dependable for others
Thoughtful about potential risks and consequences
Good at building support systems and teams
Trustworthy and honest in their dealings
Effective troubleshooters and problem-solvers
weaknesses: Tendency toward anxiety and catastrophizing
Can be suspicious or paranoid in relationships
Difficulty trusting themselves or others
May overthink decisions and freeze
Can be rigid in their thinking and beliefs
Struggle with self-doubt and imposter syndrome
May test loyalty of others repeatedly
relationshipTips: Trust in people's good intentions until proven otherwise
Communicate your fears directly instead of testing loyalty
Remember that not everything is a threat
Build a secure base but don't cling too tightly
Practice self-trust - you are more capable than you believe
growthAreas: Learn to trust yourself and your instincts
Challenge catastrophic thinking with evidence
Develop faith that most people are trustworthy
Practice taking risks despite uncertainty
Remember that you can handle difficult situations
Balance caution with openness and flexibility
Learn that security comes from within, not external guarantees

type7.name: The Enthusiast
type7.description: Type 7s are enthusiastic, optimistic, and fun-loving. They are spontaneous and versatile, seeking new experiences and avoiding pain. However, they can become scattered, impulsive, and unable to sit with difficult emotions or see tasks through to completion.
strengths: Enthusiastic and optimistic about life
Excellent at seeing multiple options and possibilities
Spontaneous and fun-loving
Great at generating new ideas and inspiration
Quick thinkers and adaptable problem-solvers
Natural ability to make others laugh and feel energized
Versatile and able to do many things well
weaknesses: Can be scattered and lack follow-through
Tendency to avoid painful emotions or difficult conversations
May be impulsive and act without considering consequences
Difficulty with commitment and staying focused
Can be superficial in relationships
May overschedule and spread themselves too thin
Struggle with accepting limitations or saying no
relationshipTips: Make commitments and follow through
Be present with difficult emotions, not just fun times
Give quality time without distractions
Listen deeply without planning your response
Remember that deep relationships require consistency
growthAreas: Learn to sit with difficult emotions without escaping
Develop follow-through and finish what you start
Challenge the belief that pain must be avoided
Practice depth over breadth in relationships and interests
Learn to find joy in routine and the mundane
Balance adventure with responsibility
Remember that meaningful life includes struggle and sadness

type8.name: The Challenger
type8.description: Type 8s are assertive, commanding, and strong-willed. They are natural leaders who value strength and independence. However, they can become aggressive, domineering, and insensitive to others' feelings in their pursuit of power and control.
strengths: Natural leaders and decision-makers
Strong-willed and confident in their convictions
Excellent at taking charge and getting things done
Protective of those they care about
Direct and honest communication
Not intimidated by confrontation
Respect strength and competence in others
weaknesses: Can be aggressive and domineering
May be insensitive to others' feelings
Difficulty showing vulnerability
Can be overly controlling and need to win
May hurt others with their bluntness
Struggle with asking for help
Can be confrontational or combative
relationshipTips: Remember that strength includes vulnerability
Soften your delivery when making important points
Ask for input from others - their ideas matter
Show appreciation for your partner's contributions
Let your partner lead sometimes
growthAreas: Learn to be vulnerable without losing your strength
Develop empathy for others' emotional needs
Practice listening without planning to respond
Challenge the belief that you must always be in control
Learn that admitting mistakes doesn't diminish you
Remember that the best leaders empower others
Balance assertion with consideration for others

type9.name: The Peacemaker
type9.description: Type 9s are easygoing, accommodating, and peace-loving. They are natural mediators who see all perspectives. However, they can become too passive, lose their sense of self in accommodating others, and avoid necessary conflict.
strengths: Excellent mediators and peacemakers
Accepting and non-judgmental toward others
Calm and steady presence in chaos
Good listeners who truly hear others
Flexible and adaptable to different situations
Even-tempered and rarely angry
Supportive and encouraging to those around them
weaknesses: Can be too passive and conflict-avoidant
May lose their own opinions and identity
Difficulty asserting needs and boundaries
Tendency to go along with others to keep peace
May be unmotivated or lack direction
Can appear indifferent or lazy
Struggle with decision-making and prioritization
relationshipTips: Express your own needs and opinions, not just go along
Take stands even if it risks temporary conflict
Communicate directly about what you want
Remember that your perspective matters
Sometimes saying no is an act of love
growthAreas: Learn to assert your needs and opinions clearly
Develop a stronger sense of self and personal priorities
Challenge the belief that conflict is always bad
Practice standing up for yourself calmly
Remember that your voice and choices matter
Learn that healthy relationships include disagreement
Find your own direction and motivations independent of others
